newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Jan 8.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - Jan 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Due to relentless investor selling, mostly by United States investment funds, which has knocked five per cent off the value of gold bullion in the past few days - to a level below the key support level of US$360 an ounce - the gold market yesterday fell to its lowest level since October 1993. Page 1.

Providing further evidence that the retail sector is in severe difficulty, Country Road Ltd and Just Jeans Ltd have announced that their first-half profits could slump more than 50 per cent. The news follows David Jones' equally pessimistic statement on Friday and the release of official retail figures for November yesterday, which showed a third monthly trend fall in sales. Page 1.

Following the release of Australian Bureau of Statistics' building approval figures yesterday, economists have suggested a gentle recovery in the housing sector is underway. The figures showed building approvals fell a seasonally adjusted 1.6 per cent in November after a revised 12.8 per cent increase in the previous month and the trend estimate was up 1.1 per cent in the month. Page 3.

Canadian gold group Placer Dome Inc is set to drop its A$423 million bid for Highlands Gold Ltd and has agreed to pay A$316.1 million for Highlands' 25 per cent stake in the Porgera mine in Papua New Guinea. The offer is well above Placer's original offer of A$276.8 million and is subject to final approval for a A$160 million underwriting agreement with broking houses Wilson HTM and McIntosh Securities. Page 13.

The two biggest global water utilities to hit Australia, Compagnie General des Eaux and Lyonnaise des Eaux, are lobbying Sydney Water to give the private sector large contracts, amidst uncertainty over plans by water authorities to farm out major capital projects. Page 13.

After a banking syndicate last week withdrew its A$15 million credit line designed to cover the potential winnings of high stakes junket gamblers at the Reef Casino RCT.AX, Casinos Austria International Ltd said yesterday it was prepared to pay some of a planned A$40 million capital injection into the loss-making Reef Casino Trust, but as only a 13 per cent shareholder the company did not believe it should shoulder all the costs. Page 15.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In an extreme response to the tumbling gold price, analysts said yesterday there was little prospect of any short-term improvement in the outlook for the yellow metal, with some predicting it would drop as low as US$330 an ounce by June - a result which has seen investors wiping A$1.3 billion off the market value of Australian gold producers in just four days. Page 19.

As a result of poor sales over the Christmas trading period, upmarket clothing retailers Country Road Ltd and Just Jeans Holdings Ltd yesterday joined giant retailer David Jones in forecasting a 50 per cent drop in first-half profits. The two retailers made their announcements after the close of trade on the Australian Stock Exchange and investors are expected to take a dim view of the anticipated slump in earnings. Page 19.

Stockbroking firms McIntosh and Wilson HTM have three days to ensure the success of a A$316.1 million deal between Placer Dome Inc and Highlands Gold Ltd, which would see Placer buying Highlands' 25 per cent stake in the Porgera Gold mine in Papua New Guinea at a return of 65 cents-a-share to Highlands shareholders. Page 19.

FH Faulding Ltd will be unable to sell its Kadian slow-release morphine drug - the first drug to be developed by an Australian company to be approved by the US Food and Drug Administration - in the A$505.94 million United States market if global pharmaceuical company Purdue Frederick Co succeeds in placing an injunction on its sale because of suspected patent infringement. Page 21.

In a result largely ignored by the market due to the current slump in the gold price, Wiluna Mines Ltd exploration manager Greg Jones says the company has made exciting new gold discoveries at its Wiluna underground operations in Western Australia - a discovery which he says could lead to another plant expansion to boost production. Page 21.

Woodside told stock exchanges yesterday tropical Cyclone Rachel is delaying a production test on the company's Keast-1 exploration well, which lies between North Rankin Reservoir and the Echo/Yodel discoveries about 50 kilometres south-west of the North Rankin production platform, which could determine if a major new gas reservoir has been discovered on the North West Shelf. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In an announcement that has surprised analysts, apparel retailers Country Road and Just Jeans have joined upmarket retailer David Jones in warning that their half-year profits would be down by 50 per cent as a result of poor Christmas retail trading conditions. The two made their announcements yesterday after the sharemarket closed. Page 14.

A decision on whether St George Bank's A$2.6 billion takeover offer for Advance Bank gets crucial court approval - Supreme Court Judge Justice Kim Santow yesterday expressed serious reservations about the deemed proxy clause in the deal - is expected tomorow and, if the deal gets the go ahead it will be largely due to the fact that National Australia Bank abstained its vote, rather than using its stake against the deal. Page 14.

Spurred on by the view that the Seven Network's profits would grow strongly in the second half of the year due to recent interest rate cuts and expectations that the group's largest shareholder, Kerry Stokes, would seek to increase his stake, Seven's shares hit their highest level since February 1994 yesterday - rising five cents to A$4.30 on more than 2.8 million shares changing hands. page 14.

Federal Court judge Justice Hill has found that the Commonwealth Bank breached a contract and acted in its own interest by favouring one customer over another in a A$470,000 joint venture between two earth-moving contractors - a ruling that threatens to have a major effect on joint venture banking arrangements. Page 14.

Independent directors of hotel and gaming operator Ballarat Brewing yesterday rejected Sir Ron Brierley's Guiness Peat Group's GPS.AX increased takeover bid of A$2.54 for each Ballarat share, a nine cent increase on its previous offer, as Ballarat's shares contiued to trade above the offer price. Page 14.

An Australian Securities Commission spokeswoman yesterday responded to claims made in the Federal Court on Monday by the Australian Federal Police that the ASC had been reluctant last year to release liquidator John Lord's report on Alan Bond's family companies by saying the ASC will consider handing the files over to the AFP if the Federal Court rules that the liquidator is not required to hand it over. Page 14.
THE AGE

The Australian Stock Exchange's Gold Index dropped 57 points or 3.3 per cent to 1707 points yesterday following the US$3.30 slump in the New York gold price to US$358.70 an ounce. The Gold Index has fallen by 6.7 per cent since the start of the year, wit gold indexes in South Africa and the US also feeling the pinch. Page C1.

Melbourne builder-develop, the Grollo Group, has taken over the entire A$700 million redevelopment of the Sydney General Post Office site in Martin Place, in a project which involves a 32-level five-star hotel and a 27-level office building behind the resored 1887 GPO. Page C1.

Following David Jones' lead, clothing retailers Country Road and Just Jeans announced yesterday they expect interim profits to fall at least 50 per cent after extremely quiet sales over Christmas, several months of generally slack retail trading and failed post-Christmas sales. Page C1.

According to Age estimates, Westpac managing director Bob Joss is set for a worry-free retirement, with a conservative estimate of the net gain from share options and his total salary over his five-year contract amounting to A$36 million, or A$7.2 million a year and if he extends his contract for five years he can expect to see an annual after-tax pay packet of close to A$2 million a year in retirement. Page C1.

Placer Dome Inc has given its conditional agreement to a plan by Highlands Gold which would see its acquire Highlands' 25 per cent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea for A$316.1 million and allow the creation of Highlands Pacific - the company to hold all of Highlands' non-Porgera assets. Page C1.

Melbourne-based Mineral Commodities NL yesterday announced promising drill results from its White Foil gold property near Kalgoorlie, with three lines of drilling at 40-metre separations returning broad gold mineralisation at decent grade and the mineralied structure open for two kilometres to the south. Page C2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
